questions.q: If the domain of the function $f\left(x\right) = \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2 - | x |}{4}\right) + {\left(\log_{e} ( 3 - x )\right)}^{- 1}$ is $[ - \alpha, \beta ) - { \gamma }$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$y = \cos^{- 1}\left|\dfrac{2 - \left|x\right|}{4}\right| + log{\left(3 - x\right)}^{- 1}$

$⇒ - 1 \le \left|\dfrac{2 - \left|x\right|}{4}\right| \le 1$

$⇒ - 4 \le 2 - \left|x\right| \le 4$

$⇒ - 6 \le - \left|x\right| \le 2$

$⇒ - 2 \le \left|x\right| \le 6$

$⇒ \left|x\right| \le 6$

$⇒ - 6 \le x \le 6 . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, $3 - x > 0\text{and}3 - x \ne 1$

$⇒ x \ne 2 . . . \left(ii\right)$ and $x < 3 . . . \left(iii\right)$

Using $\left(i\right), \left(ii\right)\text{and}\left(iii\right)$ we get,

$⇒ x \in [ - 6, 3 ) - \left\{2\right\}$

So, on comparing with $x \in [ - \alpha, \beta ) - \left\{\gamma\right\}$ we get,

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11$

questions.q: For& $x \in \mathbb{R},$~two real valued functions~$f  \left(x\right)$~and~$g  \left(x\right)$~are such that,~$g ( x ) = \sqrt{x} +1$~and~$fog  \left(x\right) = x + 3 - $\sqrt{x} .~Then~$f\left(0\right)& is equal to& $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have been given that

$f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = x + 3 - \sqrt{x}$

$⇒ f ( \sqrt{x} + 1 ) = x + 3 - \sqrt{x}$

Put~$\sqrt{x} + 1 = t$

$\sqrt{x} = t - 1$

$x = ( t - 1{)}^{2}$

$⇒ f ( t ) = ( t - 1{)}^{2} + 3 - ( t - 1 )$

$⇒ f ( 0 ) = 1 + 3 + 1 = 5$

Hence this is the correct option.

Then, the function $f + g$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f, g: N - \left\{1\right\} \to N$~defined as

$f\left(a\right) = \alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the maximum power of those primes $p$ such that $p^{α}$~divides a.

$g\left(a\right) = a + 1$

Now, $f\left(2\right) = 1, g\left(2\right) = 3 ⇒ \left(f + g\right)\left(2\right) = 4$

$f\left(3\right) = 1, g\left(3\right) = 4 ⇒ \left($f + g\right)\left($3\right) = 5$

f\left($4\right) = 2, $g\left($4\right) = 5 ⇒ \left($f + g\right)\left($4\right) = 7$

f\left($5\right) = 1, g \left(5\right) = 6 ⇒ \left(f + g\right) \left(5\right) = 7$

We can see~\left(f + g\right)\left(5\right) = \left(f + g\right)\left(4\right)$, so$f + g$ is not one-one function

Now, again we can see~${f}_\min = 1, {g}_\min = 3$

So, there does not exist any $x \in N - \left\{1\right\}$ such that \left(f + g\right)\left(x\right) = 1, 2, 3$

$∴ f + g is not onto

So function is neither one-one nor onto.

$

$= f ( 1 + 1 ) + f ( 1 )$

$⇒ f ( 1 ) = 3$

$∴ f ( 2 ) = f ( 1 + 1 ) = f ( 1 ) + f ( 1 ) = 6$

Now,

$f ( 2 ) \cdotf ( 3 ) = ( 6 ) ( 9 ) = 54

questions.q: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$~be defined as $f\left(x\right) = x - 1$ and~$g: R \to \left\{1, - 1\right\} \to \mathbb{R}$~be defined as $g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x2}{x^{2} - 1}$. Then the function $fog$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$fog \left($x\right) = f \left(g \left($x\right)\right)= f\left(\dfrac{x2}{x^{2} + 1}\right)

=\dfrac{x2}{x^{2} + 1} -$1= $\dfrac{x^{2} - x^{2} - 1}{x^{2} + 1}~=\dfrac{- 1}{x^{2} + 1}

We know that,~$0 ≤ x^{2} < \infty , \forall x \in R$

$⇒ 1 \le x^{2} + 1 < \infty , \forall x \in R$~$⇒ 1 \ge \dfrac{1}{x^{2} + 1} > 0, \forall x \in R⇒ - 1 \le \dfrac{- 1}{x^{2} + 1} < 0, \forall x \in R$

So, range of $fog \left(x\right)$ is \left[-1, 0\right) ⊂ R$.

~Hence, the function $fog\left(x\right)$ is into function and~$fog\left(-x\right) = f\left(g\left(-x\right)\right) = $\dfrac{- 1}{ \left(-x\right)2 + $1}=\dfrac{-$1}{x^{2} + 1} =$f\left(g\left(x\right)\right)$

$∴ fog \left($x\right)$~is an even function. So, it is a many one function.

Hence,~$fog \left(x\right)$& is neither one-one nor onto function.

$

questions.q: Let& $f  \left(x\right)$~be a function such that~$f \left(x + y\right) = f  \left(x\right)\cdotf\left(y\right)$~for all $x, y \in N$, If $f\left(1\right) = 3$~and $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}f\left(k\right) = 3279$,~then~the value of~$n$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(x + y\right) = f \left($x\right)$\cdotf \left(y\right)$~and~f \left(1\right) = 3$~

Now taking~$x = 1 \text{ and } y = 1$~we get,

$f\left(1 + 1\right) = f \left(1\right)$\cdotf \left($1\right) ⇒ $f\left($2\right) = {3}^{2}$

Similarly~f\left($2 + 1\right) = $f\left($2\right)$\cdotf\left($1\right) ⇒ $f\left($3\right) = {3}^{2} $\times$3 = {3}^{3}$

And so on~f\left($n\right) = {3}^{n}$

So,~$\mathop{∑}_{r = $1}^{n}f\left($r\right) = 3279$

$⇒ $f\left($1\right) + $f\left($2\right) + $f\left($3\right) . . . . . . . $f\left($n\right) = 3279$

$⇒ 3 + {3}^{2} + {3}^{3} . . . . . . . + {3}^{n} = 3279$

$⇒ 3 $\times $\dfrac{{3}^{n} - 1}{3 - 1} =3279$

$⇒ \dfrac{{3}^{n} - 1}{2} =1093$

$⇒ {3}^{n} - 1 = 2186$

$⇒ {3}^{n} = 2187$

$⇒ {3}^{n} = {3}^{7}$

$⇒ n = 7$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - x}\right) = 1 + x$

$x = 2 ⇒ f\left(2\right) + f\left(- 1\right) = 3 \ldots \left(1\right)$

$x = - 1 ⇒ f\left(- 1\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$x = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + f\left(2\right) = \dfrac{3}{2} \ldots \left(3\right)$

questions.q: Let $A = { 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 }$. Then the number of possible functions $f: A \to A$ such that $f \left(m \cdotn\right) = f  \left($m\right)$\cdotf  \left(n\right)$ for every $m, n \in A$ with $m \cdotn \in A$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(m \cdotn\right) = f \left($m\right)$\cdotf \left(n\right)$

Taking~$m = 1$

$⇒ f \left(1 \cdotn\right) = f \left($1\right)$\cdotf \left($n\right)$

$⇒ $f\left($1\right) = 1$

Now taking~$m = 3 & n = 3$~we get,

$f ( 9 ) = f ( 3 ) $\times$f ( 3 )$,

So,~ \left($f \left($3\right), f \left(9\right)\right)$~have two possibility~ \left($1, 1\right) \text{ and } \left($3, 9\right)$

Now taking~$m = 2 \text{ and } n = 1$~we get,

$f \left(2 \cdot 1\right) = f \left(2\right)\$cdotf\left($1\right)$

Now here~$f \left($1\right) = 1$, so~f\left($2\right)$~can take all~$6$~numbers,

Similarly, for~$f \left($5\right) \text{ and } f \left(8\right)$~there will be~$6$~ways each,

So, total possible function will be,~$= 1 \times 6 \times 2 \times 6 \times 6 \times 1 = 432

$

questions.q: If a function $f$ satisfies $f(\mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{n})=f(\mathrm{~m})+f(\mathrm{n})$ for all $\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n} \in \mathbf{N}$ and $f(1)=1$, then the largest natural number $\lambda$ such that $\sum_{k=1}^{2022} f(\lambda+k) \leq(2022)^2$ is equal to _________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n})=\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{m})+\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{n}) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{kx} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(1)=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=1 \\ & \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x} \end{aligned}$
Now $\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{2022} \mathrm{f}(\lambda+\mathrm{k}) \leq(2022)^2$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{2022}(\lambda+\mathrm{k}) \leq(2022)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 2022 \lambda+\frac{2022 \times 2023}{2} \leq(2022)^2\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \lambda \leq 2022-\frac{2023}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda \leq 1010.5 \end{aligned}\therefore$ largest natural no. $\lambda$ is 1010 .

$= 10 $\cdot \left[$1 + 6 + 2 + 7 + 3\right] = 190$

questions.q: Let $A = { 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 } .$ Then the number of bijective functions $f: A \to A$ such that $f ( 1 ) + f ( 2 ) = 3 - f ( 3 )$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given the set& $A = { 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 } .$

And, also a function $f: A \to A$~satisfying~$f ( 1 ) + f ( 2 ) = 3 - f ( 3 )$

$⇒ f ( 1 ) + f ( 2 ) + f ( 3 ) = 3$

Since, the range of the function is also~$A,$~hence the~only possibility satisfying the given condition is: $0 + 1 + 2 = 3$

We know that, the number of arrangements of~$n$~objects at~$n$~places is~$n ! .$

Since, the given function is bijective i.e. one-one and onto, hence, the elements $1, 2, 3$~in the domain can be mapped with only~$0, 1, 2$~in the co-domain~in $3 !$~ways~and the remaining~$5$ elements~$0, 4, 5, 6, 7$~in the domain can be~mapped with any of the remaining $5$~elements~$3, 4, 5, 6, 7$~in~$5 !$~ways.~

So, the number of bijective functions are~$= 3 ! \times 5 ! = 6 \times 120 = 720 .$
